section.title: Overview of &hanasr;
section.para: &hanasr; (HSR) provides the ability to copy and continuously synchronize an &hana; database to a secondary location in the same or another data center. &hanasr; is implemented between two different &hana; systems with the same number of active nodes. After system replication is set up between the two &hana; systems, it replicates all the data from the primary &hana; system to the secondary &hana; system (initial copy). After this, any logged changes in the primary system are also sent to the secondary system.

textobject.phrase: System replication from the primary system in data center 1 to the secondary system in data center 2.

section.para: If the primary &hana; system fails, the system administrator must perform a manual takeover. Takeover can be performed using &hana; &cockpit; or the command line. Manual failover requires continuous monitoring and could lead to higher recovery time. To automate the failover process, &sleha; can be used. Using &ha; for the takeover process helps customers achieve service-level agreements for &hana; downtime by enabling faster recovery without any manual intervention.
Multiple &hana; &ha; scenarios are supported based on &hanasr;. For variations, contact &suse; to discuss defining a PoC for a scenario that is not mentioned in the documentation.

You can use &hana; Fast Restart on RAM-tmpfs and &hana; on persistent memory if they are transparent to the &ha; cluster. On &productnameshort; 16, virtual persistent memory (vPMEM) is still supported, but Physical PMEM (Intel Optane) is not supported.
You can use &hana; Fast Restart on RAM-tmpfs and &hana; on persistent memory on &productnameshort; 15, if they are transparent to the &ha; cluster.

&hana; Native Storage Extension (NSE) is supported in &ha; solutions for automated &hanasr; in both Scale-up and Scale-out. This feature does not change the &hana; topology or interfaces to the &ha; cluster. However, unlike &hana; NSE, the HANA Extension Nodes do change the topology and are therefore not currently supported by &sleha;. Refer to the &sap; documentation for details of &hana; NSE and its functional restrictions.
